purpose: Plugin-independent implementation rules for Claude Code plugin scripts (Python/Bash) and SKILL.md: language choice, tests, placement, temp files, cross-skill dependencies, fallbacks, and version-file handling.
summary: Script language and dependency choice: Python for data, Bash for commands, standard library only
Tests required for distributed Python scripts; test naming and directory conventions
Prohibition of inline logic in SKILL.md; call independent scripts instead
Placement of scripts and docs: skill-specific versus plugin-wide, no cross-skill references
Temp files written with the Write tool under .temp/<plugin>/<skill>/ including session ID
Distributed artifacts must not reference development-only documents
Cross-skill interface is the SKILL only; shared scripts may be called directly
Delete unused code; do not use script parsers for AI-interpreted input
Do not write reflexive fallbacks; report errors explicitly
Version files and changelog are not edited in ordinary work; release procedure owns them
tasks: Implementing plugin Python or Bash scripts
Deciding where to place scripts and docs
Writing temporary files in skill procedures
Writing distributed docs, agents, or templates that reference other documents
Calling another skill or shared script from a skill or agent
Reviewing plugin changes for version file edits
title: プラグイン実装ガイドライン
